title: Ironhollow Rising
premise: Tamsin Fairweather, a mercenary sworn to the silent god Veyra, has spent years keeping his head down in the Thornfell mountains—until a smuggler's job lands him with a prophecy book that names him, by date and deed, as the one who will either break or rekindle the ancient war between the hollow-born and humankind. Hunted by the Inquisition of the Radiant Throne and courted by the last free hollow-born, Tamsin learns his silent god never died: it was imprisoned, and its silence is the only thing holding the war's embers cold. When the Inquisition moves to execute the imprisoned god and seize its power, Tamsin must choose between restoring the god he loves like family—at the cost of unleashing the old war—or destroying divinity itself. He chooses neither: he takes the god's power into himself, becoming something new, mortal and divine at once, and offers both peoples a shared future rather than a victor.
about_author: Cyrus Ravensworth is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction, and whose love of borderlands and liminal people infuses every page. He writes fantasy about those who belong nowhere—and the families they build anyway.

chapters.title: The Date That Waited a Century
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine smuggling run through Thornfell goes wrong when Tamsin shelters from a storm in a ruined shrine and finds a prophecy book naming tonight's date and his own description. The emotional beat is dread disguised as dry humor—he laughs at first, then stops laughing.

chapters.title: What the Silent God Owes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He seeks out Mother Cassia, priestess of the silent god Veyra, hoping she'll call the book a forgery; instead she recognizes the seal of the old imprisonment rites. The beat is grief: Tamsin realizes his lifelong faith was answered by silence for a reason.

chapters.title: Hollow-Born Hospitality
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Captured by hollow-born raiders, Tamsin expects death but is instead offered sanctuary by Seraq, a hollow-born matriarch who claims the prophecy marks him as their liberator. The beat is wary wonder—the enemy treats him more like kin than his own kind ever did.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dain Marrow's POV. Marrow decodes the same prophecy and begins burning shrines across Thornfell to flush out 'the named one.' The beat is chilling conviction—a man who believes cruelty is cleanliness, and who suspects the truth about Veyra's prison.

chapters.title: The Road Below
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Guiding Seraq's people through smugglers' tunnels to reach Veyra's prison, Tamsin bonds with a young hollow-born, Pip, who reminds him of the brother he lost. The beat is found family taking root in the dark.

chapters.title: Where Gods Go to Sleep
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the prison-shrine beneath Ironhollow, Tamsin speaks to the imprisoned Veyra and receives his first answer in twenty years: a single word—'choose.' The beat is devastating hope, undercut by Marrow's arrival at the mountain's gates.

chapters.title: Ash Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: Alternating Tamsin and Marrow POVs. Marrow sacks the valley shrine and takes Mother Cassia hostage, forcing Tamsin to trade the prophecy book for her life. The beat is rage and guilt—Tamsin learns invisibility was always a lie he told himself.

chapters.title: The Choice of Chains
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Seraq urges him to shatter the prison and free Veyra's full power to destroy the Inquisition; Cassia, dying, begs him to leave the god chained forever. The beat is the novel's moral crux—love pulling him in two directions at once.

chapters.title: Ironhollow Rising
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. As Marrow breaches the shrine to seize godhood for the Throne, Tamsin does what no prophecy predicted: he steps into the prison and takes Veyra's power into his own mortal body rather than freeing or killing it. The beat is transcendent sacrifice—becoming the thing both sides feared.

chapters.title: A God With Cold Hands
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, resolution. Half-divine but still human enough to bleed, Tamsin brokers an uneasy truce at Ironhollow, with Seraq, Pip, and the recovering Cassia at his side. The beat is quiet belonging—he was never invisible; he was waiting for a family worth being seen by.
